speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe when you first noticed it and if it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the infant's age, the seasonal worsening in cold weather, and the family history of psoriasis, I need to clarify if there are any areas of hair loss or if the scalp feels greasy/oily to you. Also, have you noticed any redness or scaling behind the ears or in the neck creases?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).

Based on the description of erythematous patches with greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead of a 3-month-old, worsening in cold weather, and the absence of reported alopecia, this presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis. The family history of psoriasis is a known association, and the lack of scaling in body creases (which we would expect if it were inverse psoriasis or significant atopic dermatitis) further supports this clinical judgment. No further diagnostic testing is required at this time.
